Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.

oral-bioavailability outcome.

probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: All L1 gold contexts report absolute oral bioavailability values at or above 24% or describe F as high/excellent (maraviroc 24–33%, silodosin 32.2%, odanacatib 30%, thalidomide 80–100%, tramadol 68%, aprepitant 59–67%, bitopertin high, dutasteride ~60%, vicriviroc excellent); none affirmatively supports F < 20%.

The closest structural context, aprepitant, shares the 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl ethoxy motif with the query and has measured human absolute F of 59–67% (80/125 mg fasted), including geometric mean F 0.59 (95% CI 0.53–0.65) for the 125-mg FMC capsule.

L4 aprepitant records show 10 mg/mL solubility in a self-emulsifying vehicle and increased dissolution rate for an optimized self-emulsifying formulation, consistent with the high human F values and indicating that low aqueous solubility is not an inherent barrier for this structural class when formulated.

L4 torcetrapib and phenobarbital records are formulation solubility/dissolution data in lipid vehicles or salt forms; they do not measure permeability or absolute F for the query and provide no affirmative evidence for F < 20%.
L2 low rat F values for silodosin (9.2%) and bitopertin (14–23%) are species/formulation-specific and do not overturn the human high-F direction.

Species differences in low rat F values for silodosin and bitopertin limit their transferability to human absolute F.
